caption: The drawing consists of two separate images, each depicting a hide robe with painted and beaded decorations, labeled as being from the Rio Grande Pueblos. The top image shows an irregularly shaped hide with a tan background bordered by a faint reddish-pink outline. It features four stylized birds, two at the top and two at the bottom, drawn in black and muted blue, facing inward. Across the center stretches a horizontal band consisting of a geometric bead pattern in colors such as blue, red, yellow, and white, with vertical elements that include red circular motifs spaced along its length. The bottom image shows another tanned hide robe with a faint pink scalloped edge. This hide also features a central beaded horizontal band in blue, red, and white geometric designs, with circular motifs similar to those in the top image. Above the band are two birds drawn in black and muted blue, facing each other with wings outstretched. Below the band, there are two quadruped animals (likely deer or elk), one on each side drawn in light brown and black, as well as two small stepped mountain-like shapes and a small circle near the animals. Both images include measurements "4 by 5 feet" and notes indicating "Hide Robe - Paint Bead Decoration." The bottom left corner contains the signature "Mary Berner. Dec 14, 1935." The overall composition uses muted tones of tan, blue, pink, brown, black, and red. Handwritten labels and case numbers are present near the bottom and sides of each hide depiction.
title: Hide Robes
